newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wesfarmers says year outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Wesfarmers says year outlook positive.

text.p: Wesfarmers Ltd said on Monday the outlook for its full financial year remained very favourable, despite subdued conditions in the housing industry, and the wool and livestock sectors of the rural industry.
The West Australian based agricultural, energy and hardware group reported a 51 percent rise in operating profit after tax to A$57.5 million for the half year to December 31, 1996.
Wesfarmers said fertilisers and chemicals unit Wesfarmers CSBP and rural and insurance unit Wesfarmers Dalgety made substantially higher contributions to group profits.
Gas and coal unit Wesfarmers Energy and the hardware retailing arm of Wesfarmers Bunnings recorded improved results.
However, the forest products business of Wesfarmers Bunnings continued to be affected by subdued activity in the house building sector, it said in a statement.

Wesfarmers, which is about 51 percent owned by The Franked Income Fund, said revenue at Wesfarmers CSBP rose 65 percent to A$201 million. "Flowing from last season's excellent grain harvest, demand for cropping fertilisers is expected to be strong in the second half, when most sales are made," it said.
Sales of pasture products were expected to remain subdued, due to continued low wool prices, but demand for mining and industrial chemicals should remain strong.
Wesfarmers Energy increased earnings before interest and tax by nine percent to A$48.1 million for the half year.
"The volume of export LPG sales to Japan was 66 percent higher than last year and exports for the second half are expected to be in line with the same six months last year," Wesfarmers said.
The hardware retailing business performed strongly, with sales growth of 11 percent, and the outlook for the second half was positive.
Wesfarmers said the timber market was expected to remain fairly flat for the next six months with any upturn unlikely until the next financial year at least.
Wesfarmers Dalgety was affected by weak wool and cattle prices, but had benefitted from restructuring to reduce overheads, the company said.
The overall outlook for the group was positive.
"The outlook for the full financial year remains very favourable notwithstanding subdued conditions in the housing industry and the wool and livestock sectors of the rural industry," Wesfarmers said.
